sections.title: Letter sound
paragraphs: You call this letter (jota) /ˈxota/. It makes only one sound in Spanish. You can hear it in (jugar) /xuˈɣaɾ/, which means to play. The sound is rough and comes from the back of your mouth.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Lift the back of your tongue close to the soft roof of your mouth. Keep your lips apart and push air through the small gap. Your vocal cords do not vibrate, so the voice is off. Touch your throat to feel that it does not shake.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: The letter (jota) /ˈxota/ always makes the same sound before every vowel and at the end of a word. You hear it at the start in (jugar) /xuˈɣaɾ/. You also hear it at the very end in (reloj) /reˈlox/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not say the sound like the first consonant in English jam. A consonant is a sound made when the mouth blocks or narrows the air. Do not say a soft English h as in hot. Scrape the air harder at the back of your throat.
